state.decision: Classify a change to the render engine's per-frame work for animated paths (row 11.112), made on 24 Nov 2026 after a jevgrep search pointed at it.
state.before: For every animated layer, on every frame, the engine copied the whole evaluated scene document (all objects, the timeline with every keyframe and path channel) and then replaced its objects with a copy of the one object being redrawn.
state.after: The engine copies the one object, swaps it in as the document's only object for the duration of the redraw, and puts the real object list back afterwards, through a guard that also puts it back if the redraw panics. The document a redraw sees is the same as before. Only the prepare step (once per publication) still copies the whole document.
state.measured: Debug build, a scene of 2,000 shapes with 200 eight-key path channels: copy of the document 6.8 ms per frame per animated layer before, 1.3 microseconds after. Tests: the document is unchanged after a redraw and after a panic inside one; the existing animated path tests (CPU reference and GPU) still pass.

kind.instructions: What kind of change is this?

criteria.A: A behaviour-preserving performance change: same pixels, less work per frame.
criteria.B: A behaviour change: what is drawn can differ.
criteria.C: A refactor with no measurable performance effect.

risk.instructions: What is the main risk of the new approach, and is it handled?

criteria.A: The document's objects could be left swapped out if the redraw fails part way; handled by the guard and a test that panics in the middle.
criteria.B: Another thread could read the document while it holds one object; not handled.

record.instructions: Should this be recorded in the build plan under row 11.112 (animated paths) with the measurement, rather than as a new row?

criteria.true: Yes: it is part of 11.112's per-frame redraw, recorded there with the numbers.
criteria.false: No: it needs a row of its own.
